column1: # Acceptance target routing, judge-only. One row per id of forms/targets.tsv; id is the only repeated column.

# engine: the shared engine or scenario family, a closed word; what each executes: run — the scenarios.tsv of the first directory or, when that directory holds no scenarios.tsv, its seams.tsv through the seam adapter protocol of the common README, never both; seams — the seams.tsv of the first directory through the seam adapter protocol of the common README, also when that directory holds a scenarios.tsv, which this word does not execute; extra — the rows of forms/extra.tsv of the lesson of the target (Platform/NN-<process>/forms/extra.tsv) for the target: a probe runs as the scenario of its id in the files of tables, a probe without one is not_executed (no_machine_form), a precondition runs first (scenarios none); l06 — the scenarios.tsv of the first directory and the rows of the files of tables; l11, store_group, power_stand — the scenarios.tsv of the first directory; verdicts — the verdicts.tsv of the first directory with its classes.tsv and diagnostics.tsv, by the form «Loader verdicts»; puts — the puts.tsv of the first directory and the files of tables, by the form «Installation sequences»; variants — every variant directory of variants/ of the first directory, by the form «Rights variants»; the three forms are in the section «Command tables» of the common README and their scenarios is all; vector — the rows that the wire form (Platform/common/vectors/wire.tsv) or the form of probe tables (Platform/common/vectors/probe-tables.tsv) assigns to the package; production — the rows of forms/production.tsv of the lesson of the target (Platform/NN-<process>/forms/production.tsv), the inventory of N6 of the judge norms; the directories hold only inputs (scenarios none).

# acceptance: JSON array of repository-relative directories. The first holds the executable table of the target and scenarios applies to it alone; the others hold only inputs of that table and of the files of tables; an engine word makes no directory executable. For vector the directories locate the tables and fixtures of the package.
# scenarios: all | none | first-step:<directive> | not-first-step:<directive> | range:<first>-<last> (the number prefix of a scenario name).
# tables: JSON array of repository-relative files whose rows the target executes besides the table of its first directory, [] for none. Each line of such a file
# other than its header line, empty lines and lines that begin with # is one case of the inventory, identified by the file and the number of its physical line;
# the README of the directory of the file says how a row runs.
# parts: JSON array of {key,owner}, the parts of other lessons in the stand of this target.

# body: the comparison mode of an answer body of the forms <code> <JSON> and @oneof («Expectation» of the dictionary of the common README): whole or subset for the engine words run, seams, extra, l06, l11, store_group and power_stand;
# - for vector, production, verdicts, puts and variants, whose rows are not HTTP steps; another value is a data error. The mode is a word of the row: a lesson or a chapter name sets no mode.
# role: the initial role of the doors store and store@<id> of the scenarios of the target: a role of the rights file of the stand, through whose socket <role>.sock these steps go until an @as;
# @as — the first @as of each scenario sets the role, and a step of these doors before it is a data error of the row; - — the target has no such doors in its table (vector, production,
# verdicts, puts and variants rows among them). keys.role of a profile does not replace it; a lesson or a chapter README sets no role.
# free: JSON array of the unnamed fields that the mode whole admits in the root object of an answer body, closed words, [] for none; a field that an expectation names is compared as
# every named field. error — an unnamed error is admitted with any value in the root object of the body and nowhere else. size — an unnamed size is admitted only in the root object of
# the body of an answer whose expectation has the code 413 and the kind toolarge (the body refusal body_limit of the refusal catalogue forms/refusals.tsv of the lesson), and there it
# is an integer JSON number, not a string and not a boolean, equal to the known full entity-body size in bytes; it is then excluded from the comparison. A valid, representable
# Content-Length defines that full size even for an early answer after only a prefix has been sent. Its value is decimal 1*DIGIT, with leading zeros admitted;
# permitted normalization of repeated identical valid lengths to one value does not make that size unknown. Invalid or conflicting framing lengths do not define a full size.
# Transfer-Encoding: chunked ignores Content-Length: a completed chunked body has the sum of decoded chunk-data bytes, excluding chunk framing and trailers;
# an incomplete chunked body has unknown full size and no size field. Without either framing header a request has full body size 0. A refusal for an unrepresentable
# framing length has no size field either; the judge does not impose its own integer ceiling on a candidate. Absence remains admissible when the full size is known.
# Another unnamed field, in the root or deeper, is a mismatch of the mode whole. A nonempty array in a row whose body is not whole is a data error; a lesson or a chapter README admits no field.
# rights: the rights file of the stand store, which the runner puts into {rights} before the store starts («Launch command» of the stand): a repository-relative path of a ready rights file;
# derived:<deployment> — the file that the rights derivation command of the stand writes from the stand manifests of forms/stand-manifests.tsv with {deployment} = <deployment>; none — the
# store starts without a rights file (the command template without its occurrence of -rights {rights}; the rows puts among them); - — the target has no stand store (vector, verdicts and
# the seams of an adapter among them) or every variant of its form derives its own file (variants). A directive @rights store replaces the file for its scenario only; a README sets no file.
